scientific_conclusion: The exact Stage-67 frozen endpoint and exact Stage-86 retained pair maps close to 1.13e-16 relative L2 before perturbation. Replacing only the boundary-cell zero slope by the one-sided first difference at the wall-adjacent interior x faces recovers 1.110-1.125 times the frozen wall-to-first-face jump for all four retained dominant-node/opposite-sector cases, with no change on any other interior x face. The effect is therefore large inside that frozen subspace, but this is not a stable solver endpoint, does not establish a boundary-model error, and does not imply that q_av, convergence, or physical accuracy would improve after a solver change.
positive_findings: The Stage-87 baseline reproduces the exact retained Stage-86 pair maps to 1.13e-16 relative L2 and the counterfactual is exactly confined to the wall-adjacent interior x faces.
The frozen dominant-node/opposite-sector wall-to-first-face jump response is large and consistent across all four retained side/pair cases.
negative_findings: This is an offline frozen-state counterfactual, not a stable solver endpoint, not an error correction, and not evidence that q_av would improve in a rerun.
The one-sided boundary difference remains a diagnostic perturbation rather than an adopted boundary reconstruction.
The failed Stage-28 MUSCL endpoint remains unrecovered, cross-Knudsen extension is prohibited, and no validation claim is permitted.
No physical, collision, correction-floor, source-relaxation, transport, wall, normalization, or velocity-quadrature parameter was retuned, and no cavity solver was rerun.
